text:
infra-oncall: Heads up — apiserver in us-west2 is seeing sustained connection saturation. Proxies report lots of 503/504s and we have a spike in idle/open connections. GPU pool scaleouts are failing (504) and controller-manager is requeuing due to apiserver timeouts. paging SRE oncall.

maya: I can confirm. Controller-manager leader churned twice in the last 2m and several kube-scheduler calls are timing out. Some pods stuck Pending waiting for node binding.

jordan: quick logs show proxy sidecars returning 'too many open files' across most api-proxy pods — upstream failures not the backend.

sam: kernel reports fd exhaustion on the apiserver hosts. ulimit for the kube processes is 1024 on those nodes, which is too low for our current load spikes.

nikhil: autoscaler also started returning 'failed to allocate GPU' and controller-manager is logging 'apiserver timeout'. Looks like provisioning requests are stalled because apiserver connections are queued.

sre-bot: Deploy bot: Rolled back apiserver rollout on us-west2 at 2149991250 to previous revision as a precaution.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) increase nofile limits on hosts, 2) restart proxy pods in a controlled fashion to clear stale FDs, 3) temporarily pause heavy etcd compaction/backup jobs.

jordan: command snippets I ran locally for inspection:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=apiserver -o wide
for p in $(kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=apiserver -o name); do 
  kubectl logs -n kube-system $p | tail -n 50
done
```

sam: note — do NOT run sysctl inside containers. We need to change host settings. On the host: 
```
echo 200000 > /proc/sys/fs/file-max
# and add to /etc/security/limits.conf:
# * soft nofile 200000
# * hard nofile 200000
```
I'll coordinate on-call to patch the affected host pool.

nikhil: another datapoint — etcd compaction window overlapped with snapshot backups; snapshot sizes jumped ~2x which created higher disk IO and added latency to lease operations. Suggest throttling compaction or postponing backups for ~15m.

maya: agreed, I'm going to temporarily pause scheduled backups in us-west2 for 15 minutes and adjust compaction batch size.

jordan: can we divert new GPU provisioning to eu-central as a fallback? We should be careful about customer latency, but it will reduce pressure on us-west2.

infra-oncall: updated routing policy to prefer eu-central for provisioning requests and enabled fallback pool for non-latency-critical jobs. Monitoring policy: watch apiserver 5xx rate and controller-manager leader stability.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-214999 — apiserver-fd-saturation-us-west2. Channel: #eng-sre. Priority: P1.

maya: after increasing host file limits and recycling proxy pods one AZ at a time the file descriptor pressure dropped. Apiserver 5xx rate fell back to baseline and controller-manager leader remained stable for 3 consecutive election windows. GPU scaleouts started succeeding again.

sam: followups: 1) permanently raise nofile on apiserver/controlplane hosts, 2) add FD usage alert at 70% of capacity, 3) add a small rate limiter on compaction+backup overlap.

nikhil: I'll open a PR for routing fallback runbook and capture the compaction schedule safeguards.

infra-oncall: thanks all — monitoring will keep a close eye for the next hour, will update incident ticket with timeline. :thumbsup:
